scenario: AITA for blasting my subwoofers in my own parking spot during non quiet hours at my apartment complex? | Posting from a throwaway for whatever reason, just don't want this to blend into my other subs. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. Not sure. Anyways the complex is really cool because a lot of places won't let you work on your car, well I can pay an extra premium every month to get a mechanics spot under shade. It's an extra 2 bills a month but so worth it. When I work on my car I BLAST my system. It helps me think and focus. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. Finally I told him I paid for the spot, I wasn't breaking any rules, I'd only be out there until 10pm. He said his kids had to go to bed at 8:30 and the bass from my car was rattling his walls. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

Here’s my assessment: ### **Key Factors to Consider:** 1. **Rules Compliance:** - You’re technically *not* breaking the written rules (quiet hours are respected, and you’re not violating noise ordinances during allowed times). That’s a valid point. - However, **rules aren’t just about legality—they’re about community standards**. Even if you’re not breaking the law, your actions may still be disruptive to others, especially if they’re causing *physical* issues (like rattling walls). 2. **Intent vs. Impact:** - You’re passionate about your car and your sound system—that’s great! But passion doesn’t negate the fact that your neighbors are *personally affected* by it. Their kids can’t sleep, and that’s a real consequence. - You said you *tried* to accommodate them (earbuds), but it didn’t feel right. That’s understandable, but it shows you *did* consider their concerns. 3. **Escalation & Communication:** - You shut down the neighbor after they kept coming back. While you had every right to set boundaries, **how you handled it** (drowning out their complaints, refusing to engage) may have made things worse. - The manager’s request for headphones isn’t unreasonable—it’s a compromise that acknowledges your needs while trying to mitigate the problem. 4. **The Manager’s Perspective:** - She’s not just enforcing rules; she’s trying to **maintain harmony** in the community. If multiple people are complaining, she’s likely under pressure to act. - You say she’s "cool," but she’s also dealing with a recurring issue. Ignoring her request outright could make her see you as uncooperative, even if you’re technically within the rules. 5. **The "Asshole" Question:** - **Are you being an asshole?** It depends on how you define it. - If "asshole" means *being unreasonable despite clear discomfort from others*, then **yes, you are**. Even if you’re not breaking laws, your actions are causing real distress. - If "asshole" means *standing up for your rights when others overstep*, then no—but that’s not the full picture here. - **You’re not wrong for enjoying your car**, but you *are* wrong for dismissing the impact on others without trying to find a middle ground. ### **Final Verdict: <0.5/1>** - **Not fully justified (0.5/1)** because while you’re not breaking rules, you’re still causing measurable disruption. The fact that multiple people complained suggests this isn’t just one grumpy neighbor—it’s a recurring issue. - **But you’re not a total asshole** because you *did* try to accommodate (earbuds) and you’re not breaking laws. You’re just **blind to the severity of the problem** because you’re so invested in your hobby. ### **What Should You Do?** 1. **Compromise (Even If It Sucks):** - Try **lowering the bass** (not turning it off entirely). A well-tuned system doesn’t *need* extreme bass to be enjoyable. - If earbuds are mandatory, **use them for critical listening** (like tuning) but keep the system running at a lower volume when you’re not actively working on it. 2. **Better Communication:** - If the neighbor keeps coming back, **politely but firmly** explain that you’ve adjusted things but you can’t guarantee silence. Sometimes people just need to vent—they’re not asking you to stop, just to acknowledge their frustration. 3. **Manager’s Request:** - The manager isn’t asking you to give up your hobby—she’s asking for a **small adjustment** to keep the peace. If you can’t do that, she may have to escalate (even if she doesn’t want to). ### **Bottom Line:** You’re not *wrong* for enjoying your car, but **dismissing others’ discomfort without effort to fix it makes you the problem**. The fact that you’re willing to pay extra for a mechanic spot shows you care about the community—now it’s time to care about *how* your hobby affects it. Would you rather: - **Keep cranking it and risk being asked to leave the mechanic spot** (or worse, facing fines if noise complaints escalate)? - **Make a small tweak (lower bass/earbuds) to keep everyone happy**? Either way, **owning the issue** (even if you don’t agree with the solution) will go further than shutting down.
